simple.meaning: חָם (châm) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a father-in-law (as in affinity).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Genesis, 1 Samuel, beginning at Genesis 38:13. Its contexts include birth, family, family line, Torah, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָם (H2524).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

majorEvents.label: Birth or introduction
majorEvents.evidenceText: His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.

timeline.evidenceText: Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”
When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man who owns these.” She also said, “Please discern whose these are—the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”

His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.
She named the child Ichabod,* “Ichabod” means “no glory”. saying, “The glory has departed from Israel!” because God’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

definitions.full: H2524. cham II. חָם husband's father , see חמה . II. [ חָם ] noun masculine husband's father (Late Hebrew id. , of husband's or wife's father, so Aramaic חֲמָא ; Arabic husband's male relation (father, brother, paternal uncle), but also wife's father , etc.; Ethiopic Assyrian êmû , Zim BP 48 ); — only suffix חָמִ֫יךָ Gen 38:13 , 25 , of Judah as Tamar's father-in-law; חָמִיהָ 1Sam 4:19 , 21 of Eli, father-in-law of Phinehas' wife.
